 Leicester City player ratings vs Walsall as Will Smallbone shines to secure last 32 spot
 Callum Boyle
 Tue 10 November 2026 20:55 GMT · 3 min read Add to Preferred Sources Photo by Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images Add to Preferred Sources 
 Leicester City are through to the next round of the Jersey Mike’s Trophy after beating Walsall in their final group stage fixture. 
 Some car-crash defending from Leicester allowed Walsall’s Andrew Dallas to capitalise on a loose pass from Luke Thomas after some needless play at the back and finish at the second attempt after his initial effort came off the post.
 They weren’t behind for too long as John Lundstram equalised with an acrobatic effort after being given all the space in the world to react to Will Smallbone’s corner.
 Smallbone would then get his first goal for the club as he cushioned home a neat half-volley from Tommy Watson’s cross to give the Foxes the lead. That would be enough to book their place in the last 32 of the competition, and they will now wait to find out who they shall face. Here are the player ratings from the win at the King Power Stadium .
 READ MORE: Leicester City fans question promotion hopes as 90-point target looms 
 TalkingPoints Leicester City are through to the last 32 of the Jersey Mike's Trophy after beating Walsall 2-1. Give us your reaction…
 Leicester City player ratings vs Walsall
 Dai Cornell – 6
 Nothing much to say about his Foxes debut. Conceded a goal but apart from that, had nothing to do.
 Olabade Aluko – 6
 Solid display from the defender. Always seems to play better when he is deployed as a centre-back.
 Warren O’Hora – 6
 A shaky pass from Thomas resulted in the defender losing out and chasing back Walsall’s Andrew Dallas, who promptly scored. He improved after that and was more composed on the ball than usual.
 Luke Thomas – 5
 Played his part in a horrendous goal to concede and didn’t look comfortable when on the ball in the central areas of the pitch.
 Will Alves – 5
 Not his best game as he struggled to beat his full-back. After being left out against Oxford City, it was no surprise to see him included in the squad.
 John Lundstram – 7
 Photo by Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images 
 Turning into a real goal threat. Lovely, acrobatic effort, and was assured in midfield. Some good minutes in the tank to keep him ticking over until the next game.
 Will Smallbone – 8
 First real signs of life from Will Smallbone and his best performance for the Foxes so far. Granted that this game didn’t have the same sort of intensity as a league one, but popping up with a goal and assist, as well as looking head and shoulders above everyone else is an encouraging sign.
 Tommy Watson – 7
 Was lively in a new-look left wing-back role for the Brighton & Hove Albion loanee. Grabbed an assist for the winner and put in some decent balls into the box. Backed up his goal against Oxford City and impressed again.
 Conor Chaplin (C) -5 
 Largely ineffective once again. There also needs to be question marks about him being the captain on the pitch. Lundstram seems like much more of a natural leader and, given that he is on the pitch more often, should be the one with the armband.
 Kamari Doyle – 5
 Much quieter performance from Kamari Doyle. Perhaps he was reserving himself a little bit after a lot of football in recent weeks, with some of his passing a little off compared to usual.
 Admir Bristric – 6
 Cannot fault his effort levels and tried to create plenty of chances. Strayed offside a couple of times and looked a little rash with some of his finishing but he proved to Russell Martin that he does have something to offer and is worthy of a place on the bench at least.

 Bobby De Cordova-Reid
